footerSummary: A calmer way to record food and understand nutrition patterns.
metaHomeTitle: Notura | Record it your way. See it as it is.
metaHomeDescription: Notura is a nutrition app for logging meals by photo, description, barcode or by hand, then following calories, water, weight and progress — with PDF reports and a friends-only Community.
homeHeading: Record it your way. See it as it is.
homeBody: Log a meal by photo, description, barcode or by hand. Notura turns it into calories and nutrition you can check — and where it cannot be sure, it says so.
captureHeading: Six ways to put a meal in.
captureBody: Photograph it, describe it, scan the package, reuse something you saved, or type the numbers yourself. The one you reach for is the one that suits the moment.
methodPhotoBody: Point the camera at your plate and review the foods Notura identifies before saving.
methodGallery: Use a photo you already took
methodGalleryBody: Pick an image from your library when you photographed the meal earlier.
methodText: Describe it in your own words
methodTextBody: Write what you ate in ordinary language, including portions when you know them.
methodSavedBody: Return to your own saved foods, favourites and the built-in catalogue for meals you repeat.
methodManualBody: Type calories and nutrition values directly when you already know them and want precision.
methodBarcodeBody: Look up a packaged product and check the label information that comes back.
understandHeading: Useful context, without turning every meal into a score.
understandBody: See calories and macronutrients next to your daily targets. Incomplete estimates stay visibly incomplete instead of pretending to be exact.
estimateNote: Notura shows what it could not work out rather than filling the gap with a confident number. An incomplete day means the figure you have left is an upper limit, not a promise.
exploreHeading: When you do not know what to eat
exploreBody: Notura works out what is left in your day and suggests meals that fit it, without turning the answer into a rule.
exploreOfflineBody: A built-in recommender reads your remaining calories and macronutrients, works offline, and never spends your AI allowance.
exploreQuotaTitle: AI suggestions with the limit in view
exploreQuotaBody: When you want a personal suggestion, Notura shows how much of your AI allowance remains before you spend any of it.
progressBody: Record water and weight, then move between daily, weekly and monthly views to notice changes over time.
periodProgressBody: A longer view helps put ordinary day-to-day variation in context.
aiBody: Photo and text analysis can make logging faster, but AI-based nutrition results may be incomplete or wrong. Review foods, quantities and nutrition values before relying on them.
aiFootnote: Notura supports nutrition awareness. It is not a medical device or a substitute for professional care.
closingHeading: See the whole thing, end to end.
closingBody: From a meal you record in seconds to a month you can read, keep as a document, and share with a friend if you choose to.

productTruthHeading: What is here, and what is not
productTruthBody: This page describes a current Notura build and nothing else. Family sharing, coaching and dietitian tools, and a professional web platform are planned work rather than features, and are not presented as available anywhere on this site.
metaHowDescription: See how to add food, review nutrition estimates, correct details and follow progress in Notura.
howHeading: From what you ate to a view you can use.
howBody: The useful part is not the first estimate. It is the short review that turns it into a better record.
step1Body: Photograph the meal, pick an existing image, describe it, scan a package, reuse a saved food or enter the values yourself.
step2Body: Check the recognised foods, quantities, calories and macronutrients. Missing information stays visible.
step3Body: Change foods, portions or nutrition values when the estimate does not match what you know.
step4Body: Use the day view, then revisit weekly and monthly progress alongside water and weight records.
adjustNoteHeading: Your correction is part of the process
adjustNoteBody: A photo, sentence or barcode is a starting point. Packages vary, recipes differ and AI can make mistakes, so Notura keeps review and adjustment in the flow.
howClosing: Explore the capabilities behind each step.
metaFeaturesDescription: The four things Notura does differently: flexible meal capture, estimates you can check, PDF progress reports, and a Community you control.
featuresBody: Most of what a nutrition app does is table stakes. These four are where Notura made a different decision.
featureCaptureBody: Move between photo, library image, text, barcode, saved foods and manual entry instead of forcing every meal through one method.
featureNutritionBody: Review calorie and macronutrient estimates, quantities and incomplete results before saving the entry.
featureTrackingBody: Add water through the day and keep a weight history with clear, separate records.
featureProgressBody: Review food and tracking information across daily, weekly and monthly time ranges.
featuresBoundaryBody: Nutrition values can come from user input, product data or AI estimates. They are useful context, not medical measurements or guaranteed outcomes.
availabilityHeading: Where you will be able to get it
availabilityLine: Notura is not in the app stores yet.
availabilityNote: There is nothing to install today. When the app is published, the listing link appears here.
captureNote: Whichever way you choose, the entry stays yours to check and change before it is saved.
reportsBody: Notura builds a progress report from your own entries as a PDF — something you can read, keep, or hand to someone without opening the app at all.
reportsRangeTitle: One day, or up to sixty
reportsRangeBody: Pick whatever range you want. A single day reads as a day; a longer stretch gains trends and a weekly rhythm once there is enough to show.
reportsContentBody: Calories and protein, carbohydrate and fat against your targets, hydration, how meals fall across the day, and a weight and BMI section once you have weight recorded.
reportsGapsTitle: Days you did not record stay empty
reportsGapsBody: The report states how much of the period you actually recorded. A day you skipped is shown as a gap — never averaged away, never drawn as a zero.
reportsDiaryBody: Leave it off for a summary, or switch it on and the meals themselves are appended to the document.
reportsArchiveBody: Reports you create are saved on the device under your own account, and signing out does not remove them.
reportsBoundary: A report describes what you logged. It is not a medical document, a diagnosis, or a substitute for professional advice.
communityHeading: Shared only with the people you choose.
communityBody: Community is the friends you added by email — not a public feed and not a place to be discovered. It starts switched off, and every part of it stays a decision you make.
communityFriendsBody: They receive a request, and nothing at all is shared until they accept it.
communityConsentBody: Meal sharing and daily goal progress are two separate switches. Turning one on leaves the other exactly where it was.
communityScopeBody: When you turn meal sharing on, you decide whether it starts from today or reaches back across your last thirty days.
communityWindowBody: Community is a thirty-day window, and a post leaves it when the window closes. Your own diary is never touched: take a meal out of Community and the entry stays in your log.
communityStopTitle: You can stop at any point
communityStopBody: Switch sharing off and nothing new goes out, with nothing deleted behind you. Blocking someone ends the friendship both ways, and unblocking does not quietly restore it.
moreHeading: And the parts that hold it together.
moreBody: None of this is an extra to be unlocked later. It is what the app already does.

step5Body: Turn any stretch of days into a PDF progress report you can read outside the app, keep, or hand to someone.
step6Title: Share it, if you want to
step6Body: Community stays off until you switch it on, and it only ever reaches friends you added yourself.
featureReportsBody: Any range from one day to sixty, with energy, nutrition, hydration and weight — and the days you did not record left visibly empty rather than averaged away.
featureCommunityBody: Friends you added by email, two separate sharing switches, a thirty-day window, and a food diary that is never affected by what you share.
